classification.difficultyReason: Interpret supplied line graphs to determine solution regions, then independently confirm both inequalities algebraically.

content.prompt: In each case, use the given graph to help solve the inequation. Then confirm your answer by solving it algebraically.

spec.description: Ungrid­ded Cartesian axes and a descending line, with arrows at both line ends; only intercept values 6 and 2 are labelled.
spec.mathematics: The line y=6-3x crosses the axes at (0,6) and (2,0).
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph only; no solution region is marked.

answer.worked:
The line $y=6-3x$ is above the $x$-axis when $x<2$.

$$\begin{align*}6-3x&>0\\-3x&>-6\\x&<2\end{align*}$$
The inequality reverses when dividing by $-3$.

spec.description: Ungrid­ded Cartesian axes with two ascending lines, each with arrows at both ends. The x-axis labels are 1 and 2; the y-axis labels are -2, 1 and 2.
spec.mathematics: The lines y=1+x/2 and y=2x-2 intersect at (2,2). Their y-intercepts are 1 and -2; the steeper line has x-intercept 1.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied comparison graph only; no solution region or intersection guide is added.

answer.worked:
The lines meet at $(2,2)$. The line $y=1+\frac12x$ is on or below $y=2x-2$ when $x\ge2$.

$$\begin{align*}1+\frac12x&\le2x-2\\3&\le\frac32x\\2&\le x\end{align*}$$
Thus $x\ge2$.
